subject: ss-surgical-gastroenterology
title: Liver biliary and pancreatic surgery: cholangiocarcinoma stones pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer

steps.tx: **Cholangiocarcinoma is a bile duct malignancy** arising in 1 in 100000 adults, with cholangitis in 30 percent at presentation. Bismuth type 4 hilar disease is unresectable in 50 percent due to contralateral spread. Painless progressive jaundice with weight loss is typical in 80 percent. CA 19-9 above 1000 U per mL suggests metastatic disease.
steps.say: Start cholangiocarcinoma discussions with painless deepening jaundice and pruritus rather than pain. Hilar blocks trap bile high in the liver and invite repeated infection, so sepsis often brings the patient in. A very high tumour marker plus cross sectional imaging sorts resectable hilar disease from widely spread disease.

steps.tx: Primary sclerosing cholangitis predisposes to **70 percent higher cancer risk** in ulcerative colitis cohorts. Liver flukes and choledochal cysts add chronic inflammation in 20 percent. Biliary duplication and ampullary tumours mimic hilar blocks in 5 percent. Cholangiocarcinoma shows early submucosal spread beyond the visible stricture by 2 cm.
steps.say: Imagine chronic bile duct inflammation as the soil where this cancer grows. Colitis with sclerosing ducts carries high long term risk, and parasitic flukes produce the same fate in endemic zones. Tumour cells creep under the mucosa, so a negative brush biopsy never guarantees a benign stricture.

steps.tx: **Bile duct injury after cholecystectomy occurs in 0.5 percent** of laparoscopic operations. Strictures declared within 3 months in 60 percent are usually ischaemic. Hepaticojejunostomy to healthy duct heals in 90 percent when done after 6 weeks. Early repair within 48 hours succeeds only in 20 percent due to sepsis and ischaemia.
steps.say: See how gallbladder surgery creates bile duct injury through misidentification of anatomy. Sepsis and bile leak dominate the early course, while late strictures reflect ischaemia. Delayed reconstruction to healthy duct after sepsis settles gives durable healing, whereas urgent repair in infected tissue usually fails again.

steps.tx: Acute gallstone pancreatitis resolves in **80 percent with conservative care** after 3 days of fluids. Necrosis develops in 20 percent and declares by day 4 on CT. Haemorrhagic pancreatitis carries 30 percent mortality with organ failure. Mild attacks show amylase above 1000 IU per L in 40 percent of cases.
steps.say: Examine acute pancreatitis for the gallstone proportion that settles with fluids and pain relief alone. Necrosis is not a day one diagnosis, so early CT misleads. Persistent organ failure beyond two days drives mortality, while transient failure that recovers quickly follows a kinder course.

steps.tx: **Infected necrosis appears in 15 percent** and needs step up intervention delaying surgery to 4 weeks. Percutaneous drain first succeeds in 50 percent of collections. Endoscopic necrosectomy clears 70 percent of walled off collections. Open debridement remains rescue for 30 percent with uncontrolled sepsis despite drains.
steps.say: Compare the step up pathway with the older immediate open approach. Delayed percutaneous drainage alone controls half the collections, and endoscopic clearance handles most walled off cavities. Operating too early in infected necrosis spreads contamination and worsens bleeding, so timing matters more than technique.

steps.tx: Chronic pancreatitis causes **intractable pain in 80 percent** and ductal stones beyond 5 mm in 30 percent. Cyst pseudocysts over 6 cm appear in 15 percent and cause gastric outlet blockage. Head mass over 3 cm mimics pancreatic cancer in 10 percent. Faecal elastase below 200 marks severe insufficiency.
steps.say: Discuss chronic disease through pain, stones, and failing gland function rather than single attacks. Pseudocysts that press on the stomach cause vomiting, and head masses create diagnostic confusion with carcinoma. Enzyme replacement and pain services run alongside any duct drainage planning.

steps.tx: **Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma presents in 85 percent** with pancreatic head location. CA 19-9 sensitivity is 75 percent at 37 U per mL cutoff. Double duct sign suggests head tumours in 60 percent of cases. Whipple resection for 3 cm tumours achieves 20 percent five year survival with adjuvant folfirinox.
steps.say: Review pancreatic cancer for the head predominant pattern with weight loss, new diabetes, and venous thrombosis. Double duct dilatation on imaging points to a head lesion, and venous encasement decides operability. Adjuvant chemotherapy after Whipple resection doubles the chance of surviving five years in fit patients.

steps.tx: Borderline resectable tumours encase **celiac artery in 10 percent** and replace the superior mesenteric vein in 15 percent. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy for 4 months converts 30 percent to resectable disease. Margin under 1 mm is positive in 50 percent of direct surgery cases. Exploration without neoadjuvant therapy wastes operating time in 25 percent.
steps.say: Distinguish borderline anatomy by venous contact length rather than by tumour diameter. Chemotherapy first shrinks the venous interface and tests biology before a major operation. Direct surgery without prior therapy leaves positive margins in half the cases and exposes patients to prolonged recovery without benefit.

steps.tx: **Hilar cholangiocarcinoma resection needs 5 cm bile duct clearance** and hepatectomy in 40 percent of Bismuth 2 and 3 cases. Preoperative biliary drainage reduces sepsis from 40 percent to under 5 percent. Portal vein embolisation grows future remnant above 30 percent. R0 margin achieves 35 percent five year survival.
steps.say: Consider hilar resection as combining duct clearance with liver removal to gain margin. Draining the liver before major resection prevents fatal cholangitis, and embolisation hypertrophies the remnant liver. Achieving negative margins matters more than extended hepatectomy when remnant volume is tight.

steps.tx: Complications include **pancreatic fistula in 15 percent after Whipple** and bile leak in 5 percent. Delayed gastric emptying affects 20 percent and prolongs stay by 7 days. Stricture recurrence after hepaticojejunostomy reaches 10 percent at 3 years. Post pancreatectomy haemorrhage kills 5 percent when fistula erodes vessels.
steps.say: Remember the fistula and bleeding risks that dominate the postoperative week after pancreatic resection. Delayed stomach emptying delays feeds and discharge, while bile leaks declare early with fever. Long term anastomotic strictures need endoscopic dilatation before revising the anastomosis surgically.

steps.tx: **R0 margin in pancreatic cancer gives 20 percent 5 year survival** while positive margins drop survival under 5 percent. Infected necrosis delay to 4 weeks succeeds in 50 percent with drains alone. Bile duct injury in 0.5 percent needs 6 week delayed repair. Pseudocyst over 6 cm causing outlet blockage needs drainage rather than observation.
steps.say: High-yield for the exam, remember the delay principle in infected necrosis and the margin principle in pancreatic head cancer. Bile duct repair after gallbladder surgery waits six weeks for healing, and pseudocyst drainage beats observation once outlet symptoms appear. Numbers four weeks, one millimetre margin, and six weeks anchor the viva answers.
